findings.finding: A fresh normal-kernel execution reached a nonce-bound PID 1 witness and exported current-kernel evidence.
findings.limit: This did not establish stock first-stage or Lineage init execution.

findings.finding: Stock first-stage mounted the required logical filesystems, completed switch_root and exposed the selected Lineage init in PID 1's new root.
findings.limit: Lineage init execution was not established.

findings.finding: The success endpoint was not observed; fresh ABL-associated evidence classified the preceding reset as AP_S_PANIC.
findings.limit: A successful exec followed by panic before observation remained possible.

findings.finding: The real kernel exec path, bootstrap linker and transfer to the patched Lineage executable entrypoint completed.
findings.limit: The original entry shim was intentionally bypassed.

findings.finding: The original entry shim called __libc_init and startup transferred through the relocated main pointer to patched main.
findings.limit: The original Lineage main body and Android framework were not established by this probe.

findings.finding: The frozen baseline was restored and six scoped partitions matched source bytes and expected SHA-256 values.
findings.limit: This did not claim that the restored baseline OS booted.

findings.finding: The context-closed API29 candidate reached second-stage post-fs-data and failed while applying the directory encryption policy for /data/adb.
findings.limit: Framework and UI execution were not established in this attempt.

findings.finding: One 34-byte mkdir action was replaced by a same-length comment, with every byte outside the patch span and ext4 metadata unchanged.
findings.limit: Offline qualification was not treated as execution evidence.

findings.finding: ADB was the first endpoint 21 seconds after one normal reset; second-stage init, boot-complete properties, Launcher3 and Settings were verified.
findings.limit: Camera remained unavailable and the remaining hardware and persistence matrix was not completed.

findings.finding: Clean userdata and two system-side controls still reached set_policy_failed:/data/nfc, binding the remaining caller to Android 11 init's inferred policy for Huawei's legacy plain vendor mkdir.
findings.limit: The controls identified the rule but did not yet provide a valid repair.

findings.finding: The direct vendor edit changed authenticated payload bytes while preserving the old AVB footer and authentication metadata.
findings.limit: Its endpoint is not evidence that modified vendor userspace executed; the candidate must not be reused.

findings.finding: Five encoded init bytes repurposed the redundant inferred gsi exclusion as nfc while vendor and every byte outside the exact patch window remained unchanged.
findings.limit: Offline qualification was not treated as execution evidence.

findings.finding: Complete pre/post readbacks passed and Android 11 booted with second-stage init, both boot-complete properties, writable encrypted data, Enforcing, Launcher/Settings and retained UID 0 with full capabilities.
findings.limit: Post-success reboot and the remaining hardware and stability matrix were not completed.

findings.finding: The exact target API32 VINTF implementation rejected the duplicate same-major GNSS input and accepted a source-derived 1.1-only declaration while preserving the inherited 1.0 view.
findings.limit: Target replay and host qualification were offline evidence, not Android execution evidence.

findings.finding: Two independent builds produced byte-identical system and super images; the only system payload change remained inside the existing framework manifest span.
findings.limit: The candidate was not considered accepted until complete live readback and runtime gates passed.

findings.finding: After complete prewrite and postwrite gates and one normal reset, Android 12 reached second-stage init, boot completion and a visible Launcher with vendor-verity, stable keystore2/system_suspend, SurfaceFlinger, system_server and GNSS registration.
findings.limit: This experiment alone did not prove an actual satellite fix, reboot persistence or the broader hardware matrix; later findings address some of those gates separately.

findings.finding: A bounded hardware snapshot and reversible app tests passed display, touch, GPU, sensors, encrypted storage, validated Wi-Fi, Bluetooth discovery, Widevine L1 instantiation, camera preview/JPEG and nonzero microphone capture.
findings.limit: Actual satellite positioning, rear torch, Bluetooth pairing, USB-free suspend/resume and controlled acoustic microphone quality remain open.

findings.finding: The live amplifiers are NXP TFA9874 devices; missing vendor-enhanced state selected an absent Cirrus path. A four-byte detector candidate returned the stock ODM-only value, selected generic speaker protection and restored audible mono/stereo playback.
findings.limit: The proprietary vendor library is not distributed, and transient live acceptance did not by itself prove persistence.

findings.finding: A hash-gated root-managed single-file bind survived cold boot, produced the accepted live detector hash before Audio HAL startup and retained root, Enforcing, radios and volume without a partition write.
findings.limit: The post-persistence left/right frame sequence passed machine gates, but a separate human confirmation of that exact persistent-boot sequence was not recorded.

findings.finding: Systemless read-only mounts registered GSF, Google Play services and Play Store as privileged system packages, and a real Google account was added while root, Enforcing and the speaker layer remained active.
findings.limit: No account identifier, credential or token is published; application download, Play Protect certification and Play Integrity are not claimed.

findings.finding: A removable Android VPN profile exposed two selectable private paths; both returned HTTPS 204 through the tablet core with distinct public egress identities.
findings.limit: The client package, private profile, server addresses, credentials and infrastructure details are excluded from this repository.

findings.finding: A fresh Chrome request reached GMS FIDO2 privileged API149 but failed the API32 STORAGE permission precheck. Granting GMS only READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE restored the authentication UI, USB YubiKey CTAP2 assertion and owner-confirmed ChatGPT login.
findings.limit: This finding is bound to the installed API32/GMS combination; no credential identifiers, assertions, PIN, account material or raw capture is published.

findings.finding: Termux already had APatch authorization, but its su wrapper required a filesystem su inode that this kernel-intercepted environment lacked. An app-local wrapper invoking the existing /system/bin/kp entrypoint returned UID 0 in a UID-level harness.
findings.limit: The harness inherited a privileged SELinux domain. Real Termux app-domain and foreground-terminal acceptance remain unproved; no system or root-policy change is claimed.

current_boundary: reboot-persistent API32 with most hardware surfaces, systemless speaker compatibility, Google account addition, two-path local VPN and browser USB security-key login accepted; satellite fix, USB-free suspend, torch, pairing and long-duration stability remain open
not_claimed: Play Protect certification or Play Integrity
compatibility with a release newer than API32
